task.name: No coverage that agent group-kill survives the platform sandbox wrapper
task.story_text:
## What and why

Since #1907, every Claude dev invocation whose profile does not set `sandbox_mode: none` is executed through the platform sandbox wrapper, so the runner no longer spawns the CLI directly — there is an extra process between the runner and the agent.

The tests that prove timeout and `SystemExit` unwinds kill the whole agent process group now explicitly opt out of that wrapper. `TestClaudeGroupKill` sets `sandbox_mode="none"`, matching what `TestCodexGroupKill` already did. That was the correct call for those tests: they use a fake Claude binary on `PATH` to assert group-kill semantics, and the wrapper is irrelevant noise for that assertion.

The consequence is that the process shape covered by the group-kill tests is no longer the process shape production uses. Nothing currently proves that a timeout or an interrupt reaches a grandchild through the wrapper — which is precisely where it is most likely to break, since the wrapper owns the intermediate process and the group.

This is coverage, not a known defect. No leak has been observed.

## Example

A test in the shape of the existing ones, skipped when the platform sandbox is unavailable so it stays green on hosts without it:

```
@pytest.mark.skipif(not _platform_sandbox_available(), reason="no sandbox-exec/bwrap on this host")
def test_timeout_kills_grandchild_through_sandbox_wrapper(...):
    # profile leaves sandbox_mode at its default, so _run_claude wraps the
    # fake claude binary the same way a real dev invocation is wrapped
    ...
    assert _wait_until(lambda: not _pid_alive(gc_pid)), (
        "grandchild survived the timeout — group kill did not cross the sandbox wrapper"
    )
```

The existing unwrapped tests stay as they are; this adds the wrapped counterpart rather than replacing them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test exercises timeout-driven group kill of a Claude invocation through the platform sandbox wrapper, with the profile left at its default sandbox mode rather than opting out.
- [ ] A test exercises the `SystemExit`-unwind group kill through the same wrapped path.
- [ ] Both tests are skipped, not failed, on a host where the platform sandbox is unavailable, so Linux CI without `bwrap` and any other unsupported host stay green.
- [ ] The existing unwrapped `sandbox_mode="none"` group-kill tests remain and continue to pass.

handoff.summary: Added TestClaudeGroupKillThroughSandbox to tests/test_process_group.py, covering timeout-driven and SystemExit-unwind group kills of a Claude invocation through the platform sandbox wrapper. Both tests leave ModelProfile.sandbox_mode at its default ('workspace-write'), so _run_claude wraps the fake CLI exactly as a production dev invocation is wrapped. Because the applied profile grants reads only on the worktree root and toolchain, a fixture copies tests/fake_bin/claude into tmp_path/bin (inside the allowed root) and puts that directory on PATH via _patch_env, which gained an optional fake_bin parameter. Skip-vs-run is decided by _sandbox_reachability_skip_reason, which runs the real fake CLI through the real wrapper call in an unknown mode and requires its known stderr marker — a probe strong enough to cover a missing sandbox binary, nested-sandbox sandbox_apply refusal, bwrap tmpfs-ing /tmp where pytest's tmp_path lives on Linux, and an unreachable interpreter.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
